speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you've had persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; this raises concern for a bleeding disorder. To start my evaluation, please tell me when exactly the bleeding started after the extraction and how long it has been lasting?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The family history of bleeding, easy bruising, and joint swelling in your uncle is very significant; does your mother also have a history of easy bruising or excessive bleeding during surgeries or childbirth? REQUEST TEST: Platelet count, PT/INR, aPTT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3, Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec, Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec

speaker: Doctor
text: The platelet count is normal, but your aPTT is significantly prolonged at 60 seconds, while your PT is normal. This pattern strongly suggests a factor VIII or IX deficiency. Given your uncle's history of similar bleeding and joint swelling, do you have any history of deep joint pain or swelling (hemarthrosis)?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A. The clinical presentation of post-extraction bleeding, easy bruising, and family history, combined with an isolated prolonged aPTT and normal platelet count, is diagnostic. The family history of joint swelling further supports a diagnosis of factor VIII deficiency rather than Hemophilia B.
